## 1. Expansion thesis

This plan expands attention around a small seed beside a yellow pencil while leaving the journal row intact. It offers different distances and registers for rereading the same recorded material; it does not add a new day, memory, event, relationship, quest, or system.

## 2. Story question

What can a child understand about growth when the seed cannot know what it will become?

## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_45_child_soldier_the_seeds",
  "text": "The Botanist let me hold the seeds. She said I could hold them if I was careful. I was careful. The seeds are small. Some are round and some are long and some are flat. They do not look like the thing that grows. They look like the thing that is small. The Botanist said the small thing is the thing that grows. I said how does the small thing know to grow. She said the small thing does not know. The small thing grows when the ground is warm and the water is there and the light is there. The small thing does not know. The small thing grows. I said that is like the pencil. She said what is the pencil. I said the pencil does not know the words. The pencil writes the words when the hand moves. She said yes. She said the seeds are the pencil and the ground is the hand and the spring is the hand moving. I said the spring is the hand. She said yes. I held the seeds and I thought of the pencil. The pencil is yellow. The seeds are brown and green and tan. The seeds are not yellow. The seeds are the thing that grows when the hand moves. The spring is the hand. I will watch the seeds grow. I will write the word for seed in my book. The word for seed is the next word. The Teacher will teach me. The pencil will write it. The seeds will grow it. The spring will move the hand.",
  "timestamp": "Day 228, 11h",
  "author_name": "The Child Soldier",
  "author_id": "the_child_soldier",
  "knowledge_key": "child_soldier_held_the_seeds",

  "hour": 11.0
}
```

## 14. Re-reading and variation

Use the passage bank as a set of alternatives. A single approved passage should be edited to fit its source voice and surrounding game text; do not stack all options into one entry. Keep the eight source focuses distinct, vary cadence rather than canon, and retain the original timestamp and knowledge key.

## 15. Cross-content fit

The row belongs to the canonical journal corpus. Adjacent references named by the source may guide a later continuity review, but this plan adds no cross-links, unlock order, or new narrative state. Preserve stated measurements, counts, identities, and chronology exactly until an owner reviews any discrepancy.

## 16. Failure and refusal

Reject any candidate that invents an outcome, motive, conversation, test result, settlement reaction, harvest, treatment effect, or future weather state absent from the row. Reject prose that turns an open question into a puzzle, a person into a lesson, or the source's metaphor into a gameplay rule.

## 17. Replay and callback boundary

All proposed writing is static editorial copy. It requires no random selection, replay state, callback key, persistent memory, or new journal deduplication rule. The source row remains governed by its current catalog and knowledge key.

## 18. Implementation classification

**Classification:** narrative/content proposal only; no code, authored JSON, UI route, save section, feature flag, or runtime integration is included. The local corpus confirms the row and its loader authority, not that this expansion is implemented.
